text:
maria: Heads up — auditor asked for chain-of-custody for RBAC changes since 2025-01-01. They want a signed hash proving role removals were scrubbed from prod and archived, plus a sample of triaged vuln tickets.

alex: Do they want full logs or just the delta of role_change events?

maria: Auditor prefers the role_change events (created/removed/permission_delta) + the scrubbed artifact that we sign. Also they want evidence that tickets referenced are triaged.

auditor_jane: For signature we need SHA256 + KMS signature (asymmetric). Please include verification steps so we can validate independently.

jamie: Plan: export role_change events from auth-service audit topic for the date range, redact PII, produce roles-change.json, then create a SHA256 hash and sign with our audit KMS key. Keep the original offsets. Example export snippet: 

```
# example extraction (pseudo)
kcat -C -b kafka.prod.internal:9092 -t auth-audit -o beginning | jq -c '.events[] | select(.type=="role_change")' > roles-change.json
```

Then hash+sign: 
```
sha256sum roles-change.json | awk '{print $1}' > roles-change.sha256
aws kms sign --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:alias/redwood-audit --message-type RAW --message fileb://roles-change.sha256 --output json > roles-change.signature.json
```

jamie: To verify locally the auditor can `aws kms get-public-key --key-id alias/redwood-audit --output text > pubkey.pem` and then use openssl to verify the signature. I'll include the exact commands in the bundle.

alex: Important: we need to redact emails and API keys before hashing. What's our redact step?

jamie: We'll run a scrub script that strips emails, tokens, ip addresses: 
```
jq 'del(.user.email, .request.headers.Authorization, .request.ip)' roles-change.json > roles-change.scrubbed.json
sed -E 's/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/[REDACTED_EMAIL]/g' roles-change.scrubbed.json > roles-change.scrubbed.redacted.json
```

maria: Good. After scrub we sign roles-change.scrubbed.redacted.json. Please record the kafka offsets and include a small manifest mapping events -> offsets. Auditor needs traceability.

jamie: Will add `manifest.json` with fields: `time_range`, `kafka_offsets`, `scrub_commands`, `kms_key_id`, `signature_file`.

deploy-bot: Uploaded bundle to s3://redwood-audit-bundles/1745678901/roles-change-bundle.tar.gz (size: 4.2MB)

maria: Auditor also asked for a random sample of 5 vuln triage tickets from Jan-Mar 2025 with timeline and remediation status. We'll include ticket links and sanitized attachments.

auditor_jane: Please include ticket timestamps, assignee, severity, and final status. Links are fine if we provide short-lived access tokens or export PDF timelines.

alex: I'll prepare the ticket exports (Jira). We should include the CVE references and patch dates.

jamie: Also confirm log retention policy for audit logs used here — needed for control mapping (SOC 2 CC6.2 / ISO 27001 A.12.3). Current retention is 2 years for audit logs, 90 days for access logs. I'll put that in manifest.

security-bot: Checklist updated: evidence_bundle: roles-change-bundle -> uploaded; vuln_samples -> pending. Assigned to @alex @maria.

maria: One more Q: do we provide the KMS public key directly in the bundle or a GetPublicKey response? Auditor prefers a `get-public-key` export so they can verify signature chain.

jamie: I'll include both: `aws kms get-public-key` output and a PEM file exported from that response. Also include the key policy excerpt and key rotation metadata.

alex: Regarding chain-of-custody, do we need separate GPG signing too or is KMS enough? Some auditors like an additional independent signature.

auditor_jane: KMS asymmetric signature (with GetPublicKey) is sufficient for our verification, but include any additional attestations if available.

maria: Great. I'll assemble the final bundle (roles-change.scrubbed.redacted.json, manifest.json, roles-change.sha256, roles-change.signature.json, kms_pubkey.pem, vuln-samples.pdf). Will upload and message here when done :thumbsup:

jamie: I'll draft the verification steps and attach to the bundle — include commands for `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature <(base64 -d signature.b64) roles-change.scrubbed.redacted.json`.

maria: Thanks team — pinging @auditor_jane when bundle is ready.
